what_its_for: Atogepant is used to prevent migraine headaches in adults. It belongs to a group of medicines called CGRP receptor antagonists. It works by blocking a natural substance in your body called CGRP that is involved in causing migraines. This medicine is taken every day to help reduce how often you get migraines — it is NOT used to treat a migraine once it has already started.
how_to_take: Swallow the tablet whole with or without food. Take it at the same time each day to help you remember. Do not crush, chew, or split the tablet. If you have trouble swallowing, talk to your doctor or pharmacist about options.
dosing: The usual dose is 10 mg, 30 mg, or 60 mg taken by mouth once daily, depending on what your doctor prescribes. Your doctor will choose the dose that is right for you based on other medicines you take and your kidney or liver health. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions and never change your dose on your own.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember on that same day. If you do not remember until the next day, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at your regular time. Never take two doses in one day to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store atogepant at room temperature between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep it in a dry place away from heat, light, and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep this medicine out of the reach of children and pets. Dispose of any unused or expired medicine safely — ask your pharmacist about a medicine take-back program near you.
what_to_avoid: Avoid taking atogepant with certain strong medicines that affect liver enzymes, as they can change the amount of atogepant in your body. Let your doctor know about ALL medicines, vitamins, and supplements you take, including rifampin (an antibiotic), carbamazepine, or St. John's Wort, as these can make atogepant less effective. Also let your doctor know if you take medicines such as ketoconazole or cyclosporine, as these can increase atogepant levels in your blood. Avoid taking more than your prescribed dose.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or seek emergency help if you experience: severe allergic reaction (rash, hives, swelling of your face, lips, throat, or tongue, or difficulty breathing); severe nausea, vomiting, or stomach pain; yellowing of your skin or eyes; dark-colored urine; or unusual fatigue. Also contact your doctor if your migraines are not improving after a few weeks or if you experience any side effects that bother you, including nausea, constipation, or tiredness.
when_it_works: Atogepant works over time as a preventive medicine — it may take a few weeks before you notice a reduction in the number of migraines you get. Most patients start to see a benefit within the first 4 weeks of treatment. Continue taking it every day as prescribed, even if you feel well or do not have frequent migraines right away. Do not stop taking it without talking to your doctor first.
special_populations: Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. The safety of atogepant during pregnancy and breastfeeding is not fully known, so talk to your doctor about the risks and benefits. Kidney or liver problems: Your doctor may prescribe a lower dose if you have severe kidney or liver disease. Older adults: Older adults can use this medicine, but your doctor will monitor you carefully. Children: Atogepant is not approved for use in people under 18 years of age.
